Last Friday (21st), during the verdict of the Hong Kong Alliance case, in the early hours police took away a woman who was queuing to attend the hearing onto a police vehicle. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or intentionally obstructing police officers in the execution of their duties", and "seditious intent".

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer pointed at a woman in the queue and said her "clothes were suspected of having some seditious intent", and took her away on a police vehicle. When the officer led the woman away, several officers kept directing reporters to leave, and said "take you to the press area", pulling the orange cordon line toward Yak Wa Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, they put away the cordon line. On that day, a "hearing observer" who was queuing near the woman said that she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

The Collective asked the police about the reason the woman was taken away, and whether an arrest had been made. The police replied this morning (24th) that during a security operation in the West Kowloon Courts area on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or intentionally obstructing police officers in the execution of their duties", and "seditious intent", and was being detained for investigation.
